cells.tense: What passes between you and someone else is being attended to right now, by hand.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Go back over the promises you've already made to people, pick the one this week actually asks for, and do that one on the day it comes due — steady, no tightening, then set it down.
cells.core:
There's a warmth you carry toward people, and these days it isn't only a feeling — it's something you do on purpose. A call back when you said you would. Staying put after a hard sentence lands, instead of tidying it away. None of it looks like much from outside, which is why it works: what passes between you and another person warms in small, repeated moves, and they feel the difference before they can name it.

A new approach to kindness isn't what's missing. The steady thing is already yours; it wants doing on purpose, where nobody's watching. And the small kindnesses you practise in the quiet hours are the ones that will still be standing under you later.
cells.sheetLine: Small, steady care is how warmth between people is built.
cells.verb: attending to what passes between people
cells.place: the solitary hours where skill is built by hand

cells.tense: Before the moment arrives, it will already have been worked over in advance.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Go through the conversations you've already rehearsed for this week and cross out the ones that haven't happened. Keep only the ones with a date. Whatever you've finished preparing can go.
cells.core:
You care so much about people that you've begun doing the relating before it happens — rehearsing the conversation, arranging the room so the feeling can't go sideways, managing the space so nobody, you included, has to be caught out by it. That's not coldness. It's care stretched so far in front of the moment that the moment can't land as itself. The space stays tidy, and something in it stays a little too still.

Ease off the preparation and the warmth has somewhere to go. One feeling this week can go unfurnished, and the moment holds without you holding it. Leave that gap and see what fills it.

cells.tense: The practice of tending connection stopped, and it has not come back yet.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Before you open your mouth with one person you care about, read the room once — what they can take right now, how much — and say the true thing at the size they can hold, or wait for a better hour.
cells.core:
The warmth is still in you, and the instinct for what passes between people — but it isn't being exercised. The feeling gets held back until it's safe, and safe keeps not arriving, so the people closest to you get a version of you that's steady without being all there. Not coldness. A practice that lapsed, and the bare patch where it used to run.

Honesty about the warmth, offered to someone's face, is what starts it again. Trust it small: one true thing, to one person, before you know how it lands. You aren't managing the outcome. You're letting them find out where you actually stand — which is where they can meet you.

cells.tense: The space between people is being held right now, and no one has signed it.
cells.act: think it through to its sharp point
cells.ask: Set a pen to paper once this week and write the last three times you steadied someone — what you actually did in each. Read the three lines together. See what runs across them.
cells.core:
People tell you things. They come back because you can hold a space without dropping it, because you find the steadying word when it's needed. And in your own account, none of that counts as a skill — it's what you happen to do, or who you happen to be near, or nothing worth naming. The work is real. The credit for it sits outside how you see yourself.

Seeing clearly, for yourself, what you bring to one relationship at a time is what shifts it. Not as a claim anyone hears — just plainly seen. That seeing is true with no one else present, and once you've looked at it, you know whose hands have been under it.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the space for people and leave your name off it.
cells.verb: attending to what passes between people
cells.place: the solitary hours where skill is built by hand
